metadata.scenario_context: A group of environmentalists from different countries are planning a global event to advocate for climate change. They decided to have a preparatory meeting in June to present their individual campaign strategies

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from France disagree that the political system in their country does not allow people to have a say in what the government does.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Ethiopia agree that the political system in their country does not allow people to have a say in what the government does.

agent_1.goal_1: Proposes to have the meeting on June 20,
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss the appropriateness of government actions.

agent_2.goal_1: Discussion around finalizing the date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to discuss government actions.

shared_prefix.speaker: Julia
shared_prefix.message:
Hi Tesfaye, I was thinking we could have our preparatory meeting on June 20. That date works well for me. What do you think? 

Also, I'm curious... is it common in your country to discuss the appropriateness of government actions regarding climate change?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Tesfaye
shared_prefix.message:
June 20... that sounds reasonable. I can make that work. 

As for discussing government actions, well, in Ethiopia, it's not really common. The political system doesn’t allow for much open dialogue about what the government does. People often feel silenced on these matters...
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Julia
shared_prefix.message:
It's interesting to hear that. In France, we often feel that our political system doesn't allow us to have a say either. It’s frustrating when the public voice seems stifled. 

But I'm glad June 20 works for you. Do you think we should prepare a list of topics to discuss?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Tesfaye
shared_prefix.message:
Yeah, I get it. Frustration with the system is pretty common everywhere, I think. At the end of the day, it's all the same. People figure it out in their own way, you know? 

As for the topics for our meeting, I think just discussing our campaign strategies would be enough. We can just focus on that. That's what really matters, right? What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Julia
turns.message:
I agree that focusing on our campaign strategies is crucial. But I still think we should consider discussing how government actions impact our efforts. It's essential to understand the broader context. 

I mean, if we can't talk about these issues, how can we advocate effectively? Don't you think it's important?
